reason: The text contains multiple named characters engaged in ordinary, everyday human activities. Rachel is explicitly described as a shepherdess (רֹעָה הִוא), tending flocks. Jacob is portrayed working as a shepherd and herder. Laban is depicted as a household manager and landowner. Servants Bilhah and Zilpah perform domestic work. The narrative focuses extensively on family relationships, childbirth, marriage negotiations, and livestock management—all ordinary human concerns. While these are biblical patriarchs, the text presents them within regular social and economic contexts of ancient pastoral life, not as supernatural or mythological figures.
